basis: Lightspeed led NS8's $123M June-2020 round (Bradley Twohig in tenure 2018-2021; the 2020q2 $79.4M filing is that round's paper). The company collapsed in September 2020 amid CEO fraud charges — a member with a defunct outcome, not a non-member.

Grafana Labs' original legal name (Raintank, Inc.): Lightspeed led the $24M Series A (Oct 2019), Gaurav Gupta joined the board and sits the 2021-2026 filings; the site lists Grafana (merge: raintank-inc -> grafana).
Whisper (WhisperText LLC): Lightspeed led Whisper's 2013 institutional round, Jeremy Liew board — this $3M 2013q2 filing is the round; the firm's own 2014-2017 pages list Whisper (merge -> whisper).
HQ Trivia (Intermedia Labs): Lightspeed seeded Intermedia Labs in 2015 (Liew) and his Director seat rides the 2018q1 $15M round filing; the firm's own 2020 page lists HQ Trivia (merge -> hq-trivia).
Cameo (Baron App, Inc.): Lightspeed led the 2019 Series A, Nicole Quinn board — her seat rides the 2018-2022 filings incl. the $100M 2021 round; the firm's own pages list Cameo (merge -> cameo).

Fusion-io's original legal name (Fusion Multisystems): Christopher Schaepe's in-tenure Director seat on the 2009-2010 filings; Lightspeed's Fusion-io position is site-listed and carries a fund Section 16/13G stream (merge -> fusion-io).

LivingSocial's legal name (Hungry Machine, Inc.): the firm's own 2011-2015 listings carry LivingSocial; Aaron Batalion on these filings is LivingSocial's own CTO — the membership rides the listing and Lightspeed's documented 2010-era rounds (merge -> livingsocial).

Terminal (Elastic Projects, Inc.): Nakul Mandan led Terminal at Lightspeed (his published deal list), in-tenure Director on the 2019q1 $30M filing; the firm's own 2019-2023 pages list Terminal (merge -> terminal).

Two in-tenure partners — Ravi Mhatre and Arif Janmohamed — sit the 2015q3 $7.4M filing as Directors: an unannounced 2015 Lightspeed deal. Heighten (sales-workflow software, Redwood City) was acquired by LinkedIn in 2017.
Lightspeed led Zocks' $13.8M Series A (April 2024), Arif Janmohamed board; the 2026q1 $46.5M filing continues the position (unannounced follow-on at judging time).
Tome (Magical Tome, Inc.): Lightspeed led the $43M Series B (Feb 2023), Michael Mignano board — the 2023q1 filing is that round; the site lists Tome (merge -> tome).
TollBit (Novoscribe, Inc. dba TollBit): Mignano Director on the Oct-2024 $30.9M filing, and the firm's own site lists TollBit (merge -> tollbit) — the listing plus the seat carry the membership.

fal.ai (Features and Labels, Inc.): Arsham Memarzadeh (growth, in tenure through 2025) is Director of record on the 2025 filings spanning the $48.8M/$125M/$140.5M rounds. The C was led by Meritech and the D by Sequoia; Lightspeed's participating round is unannounced in the evidence — a16z Director-pattern member, flagged for the A/B pass.

Yellow.ai (Bitonic Technology Labs, Bengaluru): Lightspeed Venture Partners participated in the $78M Series C (Aug 2021, WestBridge-led) and the earlier Lightspeed-led B; Mhatre/Wu-era seats on the 2019-2021 filings; today's card attributes the row 'both' (merge -> yellow-ai).

DualBird (Israeli data-processing engine): Lightspeed led the $8M seed and $17M Series A (announced Nov 2025), David Gussarsky's seat on the 2025q3 filing; the site lists DualBird (merge -> dualbird).
AWA (Artists, Writers & Artisans — comics/media publisher): Lightspeed led AWA's 2018 seed and 2019 Series A, Alex Taussig's Director seat rides the 2018-2023 filings ($19M max).
All Day Kitchens (All Day Technologies, Inc.): Lightspeed led the $65M Series C (Oct 2021), Alex Taussig joined the board; the firm's own page lists All Day Kitchens (merge -> all-day-kitchens).
Carta's legal name (eShares, Inc.): Will Kohler's Director seat on the 2020-2021 filings ($210M/$500M rounds) corroborates the site card's own claim of a 2019 Series E entry (merge -> carta).
Orca Bio (Orca Biosystems, Inc.): Lightspeed led the $192M Series D (June 2020), Jonathan MacQuitty's in-tenure VOP seat on the 2020q3 filing; the site lists Orca Bio (merge -> orca-bio).
Pie Tech (Houston SMB-growth AI, ex-Square founders): Lightspeed led the $19.5M Series A (announced from stealth June 2026), Aaron Frank in tenure; the 2026q2 $23.7M filing is the seed+A paper.
Arena Club (Derek Jeter's card-collecting platform): Lightspeed participated in the $10M Series A (Dec 2022) and the $6.5M A-II (Jan 2025) — the 2025q1 filing; Jeremy Liew's seat.
Composio's legal name (Sampark, Inc.): the April-2025 $24.3M round paper; Raviraj Jain's seat; the site's own card attributes Composio 'both' — LSVP participation keeps it (merge -> composio).
